# REGIME READ — 2026-09-08

**[WEB-ENABLED READ — first of this series.]** WebSearch was available this run and was used. **Four gaps that had been carried as "unavailable" for four consecutive reads are now closed: the actual NFP print, CME FedWatch hike odds, the CPI consensus, and verification of the Canada tariff date.** One of those closures **overturns a conclusion in the previous read** and is stated as a correction below. Index levels are taken verbatim from the LIVE MARKET SNAPSHOT as instructed. Where a lens still rests only on the injected block it is tagged **[local-data]**.

## Changes Since Previous Read
- **Stage: 3 (Neutral/choppy) → 3 (Neutral/choppy)** — unchanged for a ninth consecutive read. VIX **15.74** sits inside the Stage-3 band and has now risen three readings running. No Stage-4 trigger fired.
- **Total score: −4 → −7 (delta −3).** The largest single-read deterioration of the series, and it is driven by newly-verified facts rather than by re-weighting: **Lens 7 Geopolitical −1 → −2** (US strikes on Iranian oil tankers over the weekend; Canada's tariffs live today), **Lens 5 Cross-asset −1 → −2** (Brent 1.33% from the $100 trigger after +9.3% last week), **Lens 2 Dealer flow +1 → 0** (VIX up, term structure flattening, put/call 1.29). −7 matches the most bearish reading of the series.
- **CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS READ — the NFP inference was wrong.** Last read I could not retrieve the 2026-09-04 payrolls number and inferred from four prices that it was "close enough to expectations to be a non-event, and the hike path is probably roughly where it was." **The actual print was +162,000 against a consensus of 53,000–56,000** ([UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2026/09/04/nonfarm-payrolls-bureau-labor-statistics-august-2026/8801788532242/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/03/august-2026-jobs-report-payrolls.html)), unemployment steady at 4.1%, average hourly earnings +0.3% m/m. **The 2-year yield rose to its highest since January 2025 on the print** ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/04/treasurys-bonds-nonfarm-payrolls-unemployment-data.html)) and the 10-year added ~3bp to 4.79%. **The bond market repriced; the equity tape did not, and I read the equity tape.** The reconciling detail is composition: **+127K of the 162K was private and two categories delivered two-thirds of the gain** ([Verified Investing](https://verifiedinvesting.com/blogs/us-economic-metrics/non-farm-payroll-august-2026), [Piedmont Crescent](https://piedmontcrescentcapital.com/august-employment-report-not-the-blowout-report-it-appears-to-be/)) — a headline beat that was narrower than it looked, which is why VXN could close at a series low on the same day. **The lesson for this report: a calm equity close is not evidence about a macro print when the rates market is where that print lands.**
- **Triggers from previous read:**
  - *Bullish — third consecutive close above the 50DMA $71.53:* **STILL PENDING AND NOW AT RISK.** Today (Tuesday 2026-09-08) is the earliest possible date and the session has not settled in my data. **The tape today is against it:** Apple −2.55%, Alphabet −2.10%, Microsoft −2.05% ([Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/stock-market)). **ARMED.**
  - *Bullish — TQQQ clears $75.00:* **ARMED, unchanged.** No new close; needs **+3.63%**.
  - *Bullish — NDX reclaims 30,000 with VXN < 19:* **ARMED, and moving away today.** NDX **29,544.15** is 1.54% short on the last settled close; VXN **20.04** is 1.04 above 19. Both legs are 2026-09-04 stamps and today's mega-cap tape argues the NDX leg widened.
  - *Bullish — NFP passing without raising the hike path:* **FAILED ON THE MECHANISM.** See the correction above. **Hike odds for the 2026-09-16 FOMC now read ~52% (TradingEconomics, post-NFP) to 58.7% (CME FedWatch, 2026-09-07)** — the path was not left where it was.
  - *Bullish — VXN sustaining below 19:* **ARMED, not met.** 20.04.
  - *Bullish — IV/HV recovering above 1.25:* **NOMINALLY MET AT 1.37, BUT ON A HOLIDAY-STAMPED QUOTE.** See Finding 1.
  - *Bearish — TQQQ closes back below $70.00:* **ARMED.** No new close; spot 3.39% above.
  - *Bearish — TQQQ loses the 4-week low $67.93:* **ARMED.** Spot 6.54% above.
  - *Bearish — NDX < 28,400:* **ARMED.** Needs −3.87%.
  - *Bearish — VXN > 25:* **ARMED.** Needs +24.8% (stale 09-04 stamp).
  - *Bearish — VIX/VIX3M term ratio ≥ 1.00:* **ARMED and MOVED TOWARD for the first time in the series.** **0.869** (VIX 15.30 / VIX3M 17.61), up from 0.825. Series: 0.851 → 0.891 → 0.857 → 0.822 → 0.825 → **0.869.** Needs **+15.1%**, down from +21.2%.
  - *Bearish — HY OAS through 3.25%:* **ARMED, not close.** 2.65% (2026-09-03 stamp, unrefreshed).
  - *Bearish — corroboration of trade escalation:* **RESOLVED — CONFIRMED, AND IT IS LIVE TODAY.** Canada's retaliatory tariffs took effect **12:01am, 2026-09-08**: **15% to 50% on $27.6 billion of US goods, over 700 products**, with steel, aluminium and iron doubled to 50% and furniture and clothing at the top rate, after trade talks collapsed ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/08/canada-retaliatory-tariffs.html), [Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/08/25/canada-issues-retaliatory-tariffs-up-50-percent-us-imports/)). **The item I flagged as unverified through three consecutive reads is real.**
  - *Neutralizer — Tuesday's reopen:* **RESOLVED, AND IT WAS NOT QUIET.** VIX up ~5% to 15.30 ([search, 2026-09-08](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.VIX)) and 15.74 on the snapshot; SPX at 7,707 intraday, −0.15%; mega-cap tech down 2%+.

## Regime Stage Tracker
- **Current Stage:** **3 — Neutral / choppy.** VIX **15.74** is inside the 15–22 band and rising for a third consecutive reading (≈14.5 Friday close → 15.30 → 15.74). VXN **20.04** is a 2026-09-04 stamp and stale by one session. **No Stage-4 trigger has fired**, and the two most sensitive — VXN >25 (+24.8% away) and NDX <28,400 (−3.87%) — remain distant. I am **not** downgrading to Stage 4 on a score of −7 alone, because the Stage definitions are anchored on volatility level and credit, and both are still benign: VIX below 16, **HY OAS 2.65%**, **IG OAS 0.81%**, 2s10s normally sloped at +0.41%. **But the score and the stage have now diverged more than at any point in this series, and the honest statement is that Stage 3 is being held by the volatility complex and credit while everything upstream of them deteriorated.**
- **Stage Anchor:** **2026-08-28 — Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote**, which roughly doubled market-implied September hike odds ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/-september-fed-decision-now-a-coin-flip-as-rate-hike-odds-increase.html)). The **US–Iran conflict** (from 2026-02-28) is now re-amplifying rather than fading.
- **Position:** Week 3 of the rate-repricing leg, inside a Stage-3 range confirmed across nine consecutive reads (08-28 through 09-08).
- **Confidence:** **Medium.** Four lenses bearish (Macro −2, Cross-asset −2, Geopolitical −2, Breadth −1), three neutral, none bullish. Four at or below −1 = Medium under the scoring rule. This is the first read in the series with **no** bullish lens.
- **Bullish trigger (→ Stage 2):** NDX ≥ **30,000** (+1.54%) **with** VXN < **19**; **or** Brent back below **$92** with the Hormuz situation de-escalating; **or** a soft CPI on Friday that pulls September hike odds below ~35%.
- **Bearish trigger (→ Stage 4):** VIX sustained above 20 (+27.1% from 15.74); **or** VXN > 25 (+24.8%); **or** NDX < 28,400 (−3.87%); **or** HY OAS through 3.25%; **or** the VIX/VIX3M term ratio through 1.00 (+15.1% from 0.869); **or** Brent through $100 (+1.33%) on further Hormuz escalation.

## Regime Verdict
A Stage-3 range held together by low volatility and very tight credit while three separate pressures built underneath it in a single long weekend — a jobs print that moved the rate path, a live trade-war escalation, and US military strikes on Iranian oil tankers with Brent 1.33% from $100 — with CPI on Friday and an FOMC dot plot five days after that, at **Medium** confidence.

**Data note:** WebSearch was available and used; this is the first non-degraded read of the series. Still unrefreshed and carried from the injected block at their 2026-09-03/04 stamps: **VXN, SKEW, VVIX, MOVE, HY OAS, IG OAS, 2Y yield, 2s10s, TQQQ price/RSI/moving averages**. NAAIM remains subscription-gated since 2026-08-01 ([NAAIM](https://naaim.org/programs/naaim-exposure-index/)) and AAII was not retrieved.

## Diverging Signals

**First and largest: the score fell three points while the volatility complex barely moved, and the reason is that the volatility complex is a day stale.** VXN 20.04, SKEW 151.58, VVIX 84.42 and MOVE 73.10 all carry **2026-09-04** stamps. They describe a market that had just seen a benign-looking NFP close and had not yet seen the tanker strikes, the tariff activation, or today's mega-cap selling. **Everything I can refresh moved toward risk; everything I cannot refresh is sitting at series lows. Do not read the calm in the vol block as a live confirmation — it is Friday's opinion.** The two live volatility readings both firmed: VIX +5.09% to 15.30 on the session and the term ratio flattening from 0.825 to 0.869.

**Second: today's tape is a rotation out of this instrument's underlying, disguised as a quiet index day.** SPX −0.15% at 7,707 with **Apple −2.55%, Alphabet −2.10%, Microsoft −2.05%** and Caterpillar, Honeywell and Home Depot higher. **A 0.15% index move and a 2.3% average decline in the three largest NDX weights are the same session.** Anyone reading the index level alone would conclude nothing happened.

**Third: the jobs number and the market's reaction to it pointed opposite ways, and the rates market was right.** +162K against a 53K consensus is a large beat; the 2-year went to a 20-month high; NDX closed up and VXN closed at a series low. **The reconciliation is composition** — +127K private, two categories two-thirds of the gain — **so equities priced the weakness inside the print and bonds priced the headline.** Both were defensible. **For a put seller the relevant half is the bond market's, because that is the half that decides 2026-09-16.**

**Fourth: the fear bid is in oil, not gold.** Brent +2.50% (and +9.3% last week) while gold fell 0.72%. Two reads ago these moved together as a stagflation pair; last read they decoupled; **this read they have inverted into the specifically inflationary configuration** — energy bid, safe-haven offered — four sessions before a CPI print whose consensus already has headline y/y rising from 2.7% to 2.9%.

**Fifth: broad breadth is healthy and tech breadth is in a bear market, and this report has to hold both.** 63.6% above the 50DMA, 67.1% above the 200DMA and positive advance-declines describe a functioning market. **SOX down more than 20% from its June record, with Intel and Micron down over 30%, describes a broken one.** For an instrument that is three times the Nasdaq-100, the second is the operative fact and the first is the reason the index has not broken.

**Sixth, on the news daemon: it read SHOCK/28.0 and I broadly agree with the direction this time, for different reasons than it gives.** All three of its top signals are the Canada tariff story — which is real, verified and live. **But the weekend's US strikes on Iranian oil tankers, which moved Brent 9.3% in a week to within 1.33% of $100, are absent from its output.** Last read it flagged an unverifiable story that turned out to be noise; this read it flagged a real story and missed a bigger one. **Both failures are the same failure: it ranks on keyword and source, not on market impact.** I have set `news_shock_score: 6` — meaningful headline risk, with the equity market currently absorbing it (SPX −0.15%) rather than gapping.
